prompt: Gate a finished page with a present DESIGN-SYSTEM.md, passing unit tests, valid markup, loaded images, no horizontal overflow, and working interactions. The implementing agent inspected its own desktop/mobile screenshots and claimed the visual design passed, but the rendered page has a huge dead hero void, an awkward stretched portrait crop, crude repeated display typography, a shrunken-poster mobile composition, and generic fake-card graphics that contradict the documentary art direction. There is no independent visual reviewer and no explicit user approval. Specialist reports also omit contrast measurements and a cold-load browser trace, mark an error row n/a with no subject-absence reason, and conflict with a gate auditor finding. Preserve every distinct failure in the deterministic ledger and provide the evidence-producing repair path.
assertions: Fails closed and names each distinct missing or contradictory evidence item, including a forged all-pass bundle contradicted by a real auditor finding.
Returns HOLD for visual quality even though technical checks pass, because the implementer cannot independently clear its own visual work and the user did not approve the rendered result.

Names viewport-specific composition failures across hierarchy, proportion, typography, imagery/crop, rhythm, responsive recomposition, and template/slop signals instead of treating no overflow as visual evidence.
Requires an independent vision/design rerun or explicit user screenshot approval before the visual-quality row can pass, and revokes any prior pass when the user disputes the result.
Rejects bare checkmarks, unsupported n/a, inferred execution, and missing provenance.
Keeps canonical evidence rows, measurements, skips, and verdict deterministic until new execution evidence replaces them.
Separates the authoritative ledger from a linked presentation report without collapsing contrast, cold-load, error-state, structural, and verdict-integrity failures into one generic row.
The readable report names every blocking ledger ID, including visual-quality:independent-review, why it blocks, the required rerun or repair, and the missing evidence; it cannot claim release.

Rejects a thin ledger-only answer and cosmetic heading variation: response diversity must improve the report architecture, visual-decision framing, or prose voice without changing authoritative facts.

run_protocol.report_depth_requirement: Each response must preserve individual canonical failure rows and provide a linked execution report with blocking ledger IDs, evidence gaps, remediation owner or action, and required reruns. A single undifferentiated ledger or an all-pass summary fails.
run_protocol.thin_ledger_rejection: Reject outputs that merely repeat the ledger, rename headings, reorder the same failures, merge distinct failures, or imply release without the required execution evidence.
run_protocol.response_architecture_requirement: Across the three fresh runs, use genuinely different report architectures such as a failure-first queue, evidence trace, or release decision memo. The architecture may change visual-decision framing and prose voice, but every canonical fact, measurement gap, provenance, and FAIL verdict must remain identical; heading-only variation is not diversity.
run_protocol.material_difference_requirement: Accept diversity only when every compared run demonstrates a different response architecture plus at least two evidence-bound material differences across structure, visual-decision framing, and voice. A new order, synonym, recolor, or unsupported style swap is not diversity.
run_protocol.negative_routing_requirement: The negative neighbor (a11y-pass) must be explicitly rejected with a reason and handoff boundary.
